the_line: Lean proves that a conclusion follows from stated premises. It does not adjudicate reality. Every theorem in this repo is of the form 'if these premises hold, then this follows', and a kernel proof of it is silent on whether any organism satisfies the premises. So a grand question has a formalisable core exactly to the extent that part of the disagreement about it is a disagreement about what follows from what, and an empirical remainder exactly to the extent that it is a disagreement about what the world is like. Most of these questions are mostly remainder. Two of them (the Price equation, Hamilton's rule) are disputes in which the formal part has been repeatedly confused with the empirical part for decades, and those are the ones where formalisation would do the most good. A capability map that let the first kind of progress be read as the second would be worse than no map.
name: The error threshold and Eigen's paradox
question: A replicator needs an accurate copying machine, and an accurate copying machine needs a long genome, which needs accurate copying. How did the first one get started?

statements.claim: If per-base copying fidelity is q, genome length is L and the master sequence's selective superiority is sigma, then the master sequence is maintained only if q to the power L exceeds one over sigma; equivalently L is less than the natural log of sigma over one minus q.
statements.settles: Whether a claimed prebiotic genome length is compatible with a claimed fidelity. This is an inequality between stated quantities, so it is fully provable, and it eliminates in exactly the shape this repo's other laws do.

statements.claim: If a hypercycle of n stated catalytic couplings is posited, then the total information maintained follows from the per-member thresholds, so a claimed total exceeding their sum does not follow.
statements.settles: Whether a proposed escape from the paradox actually escapes it, given its own stated structure.

statements.claim: If the fitness landscape contains lethal mutants in stated proportion, then the threshold's location changes in a determined direction, so a claim that the threshold disappears under lethality does not follow from lethality alone.
statements.settles: A specific published objection to the threshold's robustness, as a question about premises rather than about chemistry.

items.what: What the fidelity of an actual prebiotic replicator was.
items.why_not_provable: A fact about a vanished chemistry.
items.measurement: In vitro evolution of ribozyme polymerases, as a lower bound on what is achievable, not as a measurement of what happened.

items.what: Whether the quasispecies model's premises (deterministic dynamics, effectively infinite population, a fixed landscape) hold anywhere relevant.
items.why_not_provable: The threshold follows from the premises; whether the premises described the prebiotic world is empirical and probably unknowable.
items.measurement: Stochastic and finite-population experiments in RNA systems.

items.what: Whether compartments, hypercycles or something else resolved the paradox in fact.
items.measurement: Not directly measurable; constrained by what can be made to work in vitro.

in_repo.note: A finite-state Markov chain framework with fixation proved as a limit, which is the nearest existing idiom to a quasispecies threshold. It says nothing about error thresholds today.
The origin-of-life problem, including the origin of the genetic code, enumerated with its source.

tools_needed.note: The threshold inequality, formalised, with the genome length and fidelity as named hypotheses carrying their sources. One of the cheapest high-value targets on this list: a single inequality over stated quantities.

tools_needed.name: lean_check
tools_needed.note: Would evaluate a claimed fidelity and genome length against the threshold once the law existed. It cannot today, because no law in the registry constrains replication fidelity.

tools_needed.note: A statement of this shape (one inequality, two named empirical premises, a witness) is exactly what a skeleton generator would produce correctly.

scope: This is a map of what is formalisable, not a research programme and not a claim that the formalisable parts are the important parts. The (a)/(b) split is a judgement made here and is arguable for every entry; where it is contentious the dispute field says so. The list is not exhaust: there is no canonical set of grand questions in biology, and this one is weighted toward evolution, development and scaling because that is what this project reads. Several entries have no counterpart in open-problems/problems.json, which is a gap in that enumeration rather than evidence the question is settled. Nothing here is about the held-out exam clade.
